youtube.title: The ninety minute day
youtube.caption:
At a day of an hour and a half you weigh about one eighth of what you did.

Part 8 of 8 of "What If Earth Spun Faster and Couldn't Stop?" — the full video is on this channel.

Sources
1. Your weight as a share of what it would be on a non-spinning Earth: 99.7% today, 98.6% at a 12 h day, 94.5% at 6 h, 78.0% at 3 h, 50.4% at 2 h and 11.9% at 1.5 h. A 70 kg person weighs 69 kg at 12 h and 55 kg at 3 h. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
2. With the same push, jump height grows as gravity shrinks: about 2 times higher at a 2 h day and 8.4 times at 1.5 h; a falling cup takes 1.4 and 2.9 times longer. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
3. A basketball hoop is 3.05 m (10 feet) above the floor; a 0.5 m jump becomes about 4.2 m when you weigh 1/8.4 as much. — FIBA Official Basketball Rules (ring height 3.05 m; find the page): https://www.fiba.basketball/
4. The ground at the equator moves at about 1,674 km/h (465 m/s): one trip around the equator divided by the length of a day. That is about 1/17 of the speed needed to orbit. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)
5. Speed of the ground at the equator: 1,674 km/h today, 3,340 km/h at a 12 h day, 6,679 km/h at 6 h, 13,358 km/h at 3 h, 20,038 km/h at 2 h and 26,717 km/h at 1.5 h. The Sun is up for half of each day. (our calculation; the arithmetic is shown in the film)

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Thumbnail illustration made with AI. Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. Every number is checked against the sources.

Possibility Lab: Impossible questions, honest assumptions, real calculations.
